source.title: Reframing Long-Tailed Learning via Loss Landscape Geometry
source.authors: Sheng-Wei Chen; Yi-Ming Liu; Yan-Zhen Wang; Yu-Jia Wang; Xian-Kai Lu

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper and supplementary material; no relevant truncation is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own measurements linking class-specific feature quality, loss-landscape geometry, and gradient similarity to tail-class performance in long-tailed learning. It refines the generalization-gap framing to class imbalance and reports results for a proposed method, but does not measure train–test generalization gaps as the listed versions define them.
record.gate_note: The paper's results concern long-tailed recognition and head–tail accuracy, not the claim's specified train–test gap on natural-label data. The cited generalization and sharpness findings are prior work. Rows below capture this paper's own measurements about tail performance and its method; they do not directly test V1–V8 as written.
record.test_reason: The study uses the premise that flatter minima improve generalization to design grouped sharpness-aware training, then evaluates long-tailed recognition. It does not test any listed version. In particular, qualitative landscapes and Hessian spectra do not measure V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its association with train–test gaps at comparable training loss, or its ranking against competing measures.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors attribute the head–tail trade-off to tail performance degradation and unfavorable loss geometry, and conclude that grouped knowledge preservation plus grouped sharpness-aware training improves recognition on four long-tailed benchmarks without external data or pretrained models.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains long-tailed classifiers and introduces grouped knowledge preservation and grouped sharpness-aware optimization; it does not use the claim's random-label, width-sweep, optimizer-comparison, dropout, or memorized-example procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: Group count changes performance: the paper reports optimal performance at G=4 on CIFAR10-LT and CIFAR100-LT, at G=4 on iNaturalist 2018, and at G=6 on ImageNet-LT. Knowledge-preservation strength λ changes performance on CIFAR100-LT (r=100), with best reported accuracy at λ=100. Perturbation scale affects performance, with the text reporting a peak at Z=10−2.

fits_no_version.finding: BCL's tail-class feature quality peaks at epoch 120 and declines; the proposed framework maintains improving head- and tail-class feature quality.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Tail-class feature quality can deteriorate during long-tailed training, and grouped knowledge preservation can mitigate that deterioration.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed method has qualitatively flatter class-specific landscapes and sustains greater tail-class gradient similarity than the reported baselines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grouped sharpness-aware training and knowledge preservation alter loss geometry and tail-class gradient contributions in long-tailed recognition.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed framework improves reported overall and class-frequency-group accuracy on long-tailed classification benchmarks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed grouped training framework improves long-tailed recognition accuracy over the tested baselines.

record.problems: The supplied Table 1 is flattened and its numeric alignment is ambiguous. The reported geometry is qualitative or figure-based, and the paper does not report train–test error gaps or test-error comparisons under the conditions specified by the claim.
record.rows_left_out: Many benchmark comparison values in Tables 1–3 are not included because the tables' flattened numeric alignment is ambiguous and the reported outcomes are long-tailed accuracy rather than the claim's generalization-gap measures. Figure-only group-count, perturbation-scale, and Hessian-spectrum values were also not transcribed as precise rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance under matched natural-label and random-label training.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove a large-batch penalty.
Dropout comparisons, training-set-size dependence, excessive dropout, and removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus train–test gaps among similarly fitted networks, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Replace the record's tests/T5 classification with uses_without_test/T4. Supplementary Hessian results also concern a different sharpness measure and supply no V7 gap analysis. The absence of train–test gaps is specifically relevant to V7; other versions are untested because their required experimental comparisons are absent.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and the resulting test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures on image generalization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and held-out performance.
Large versus small batch generalization gaps under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measured against train–test gaps and competing measures.
Removal and retraining of memorized examples and its effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: BCL [75]
rows.operation_detail: Tracked tail-class feature quality during training; it peaked at epoch 120 and then declined.
rows.measure: Tail-class feature quality Q over epochs
rows.value: Feature quality rises sharply initially, peaks at epoch 120, then declines.
rows.note: Authors interpret this as tail performance degradation; it is not a train–test error-gap measurement.
rows.check: The reported feature-quality peak at epoch 120 is supported, but feature quality does not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: our framework
rows.operation_detail: Tracked head- and tail-class feature quality during training.
rows.measure: Head- and tail-class feature quality Q over epochs
rows.value: Both head and tail classes exhibit a similar upward trend and stable enhancement in feature quality.
rows.note: This measures feature quality, not held-out error or a generalization gap.
rows.check: The feature-quality trend is supported. This is a diagnostic comparison of the proposed method, not evidence for a listed version.

rows.subject: BCL [75]
rows.operation_detail: Compared loss-landscape geometry for head and tail classes after learning.
rows.value: Tail classes have sharp loss landscape geometry.
rows.note: No perturbation tolerance or train–test gap is reported.
rows.check: The qualitative sharp tail-class landscape is reported, but cannot establish V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap relation.

rows.subject: our method
rows.operation_detail: Compared loss-landscape geometry for head and tail classes after learning.
rows.value: Our method has a flat region for both tail classes and head classes.
rows.note: This qualitative landscape finding does not establish the magnitude-aware sharpness and gap relation in V7.
rows.check: The flatter landscape is reported for the proposed method. Neither magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance nor train–test gaps are measured.
